comments.author: CaptLowside
comments.body_html:
SPT tends to use physical cores for processing. If your CPU is maxing out a couple of cores only but is barely using others, it will show total CPU usage as a percentage (50% in your case) then you may still still be bottlenecked.
Use CPU-Z or similar to track individual core usage.

comments.author: peznov369
comments.body_html:
Do you need me to give some screenshots to prove what I’m saying? Perhaps it works with your computer configuration, but it does not work on mine.

It’s important that the mod author understands clearly what I’m saying. If I am playing on 4k with FSR 3.0 active, then the image is absolutely identical regardless of the slider or the other mod settings. The second I disable FSR And instead use TAA or FXAA or no AA whatsoever, the slider has an obvious and extremely noticeable effect, and a significant impact on FPS.

The fact that you are suggesting that you need to closely compare the presets by looking at a fence makes me think that in fact you are just seeing the placebo effect, because the effects are extremely aggressive and dramatic if you turn FSR off. The slider being at 100%, for example, literally turns everything outside of your scope to a near complete blur. That is what the mod can look like when it is properly working. If it doesn’t look like that for you when you set the slider to 100%, then it isn’t really working.
